provenance.source: PR #11087 fix(interceptors): trim trailing ejected handlers, squash-merged 2026-07-29 as 712e02373
provenance.note: Introduced by this PR: it added a bookkeeping pass that runs at the top of `use`, `eject` and `forEach` and reads `handlers.length` before anything checks that the public `handlers` value exists. The field has always been a plain public array that callers assign to, and the class's own `clear()` still guards it with `if (this.handlers)`, so a falsy value was a tolerated no-op for iteration before this PR; now the first `forEach` of the next request throws. The later fix #11118 adds a count helper that treats a nullish value as empty and re-creates the array in `use`, closing issue #11114, which reports `axios.interceptors.request.handlers = null` throwing `Cannot read properties of null (reading 'length')` on every request. The `use()` throw on a nullish stack is older than this PR (the array push was unguarded before it); the iteration crash is new, and the fix touches both lines the case anchors.

keywords: a falsy public list makes every request throw
every request crashes once the public array is falsy
user code that nulls the public array crashes the next request
crashes when the public collection is replaced with a falsy value
does not tolerate a caller-assigned falsy collection
rejects a replaced collection instead of treating it as empty
bugs.note: the sync pass dereferences the public handler array before any existence check, so a caller that replaces it with a falsy value turns every later request into a TypeError; the fix counts through a helper that treats a nullish value as empty
